targets.title: What can policy-makers do to increase the effectiveness of building renovation subsidies?
targets.evidence_quote:
We
replicate a Swiss study on free-riding prevalence in household energy retrofitting in Norway Studer
and Rieder (2019).
targets.outcome_quote:
Compared to the original studies free-riding prevalence of 50%, we find only 10%, indicating that Norwegian free-riding is low. Similar to the original study, we find that the use of advisory
service and having a good perception of the implementer is associated with not free-riding, but argue
these findings should not be interpreted entirely causally, as confounding variables can also explain this
association.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors contrast prevalence of 10% with original 50%, while explicitly confirming associations with advice services and implementer perception. They retest the first two studies of the same original paper; focus-group study is omitted.

reasoning: Title, authors and DOI verified in complete 10-page article including references. One original paper re-tested with Norwegian household survey data. Rieder 1999 and other prevalence research are background.
